body:
Measurement from PR #77's review, recorded here so whoever picks this up knows what already exists and what is unverified.

**Three microprograms already emit `NVM_MARK`** — `SET_CONFIGURATION` (`gen_ucode.py` `E_SCFG`), `SET_SAMPLING_RATE` and `SET_CLOCK_SOURCE`. The op drives `eff_nvm_stb_o` out of the uCPU (`KL_aecp_ucpu.sv:420`) and `eff_nvm_mark_o` alongside it.

**Both terminate in a no-connect at the top**: `protocol_processor_top.sv:2821-2822` binds them to `aecp_eff_nvm_mark_nc_w` / `aecp_eff_nvm_stb_nc_w`. So the marks are emitted, correct as far as anyone can tell, and observable by nothing.

Consequence for testing, which is the part worth writing down: **deleting `NVM_MARK` from any of the three programs is silent.** Verified — dropping it from `E_SCFG` leaves all 484 `tb/pp_top` checks green. That is not a defect in those programs; there is simply no consumer to observe, and a test that pinned the strobe would grade microcode structure rather than behaviour.

So this issue owns two things, not one:

1. the flash backend itself, and
2. **connecting and grading the marks that are already being emitted** — once `eff_nvm_stb_o` reaches something, the three existing call sites become gradeable end to end, and the persistence claim in `es-5.1` becomes provable rather than asserted.

Worth doing them together: wiring the backend without grading the marks would leave the same false-success shape this issue already describes for `A_PP_STAT`.

Scope correction from an RTL-angle review of protocol-processor PR #13, so this ticket does not read as closed by it.

**The desk-proof sentence here is "leave the previous saved set intact", and the NVM port layer cannot meet it.** PR #13 pins "a torn commit leaves every OTHER record untouched", which is honest and is what the port can guarantee, but it is weaker precisely on the record being rewritten. The destructive window is also the whole commit rather than just the WRITE: a cut at `S_WWREQ` errs with zero bytes on the bus and the erase already advanced, so **`err` never means the saved set is unchanged**.

Covering the record being rewritten needs the crc16 (specified, not implemented) or A/B promotion. The flash map's A/B slots are per record SET, whole-image with read-back-then-promote; this port has no slot notion.

Four defects found in the same review and filed against the protocol-processor: unowned `done_seen_r` (#14), no timeout so a silent device wedges the port (#15), restore failures collapsing three situations into one signal against `GAPS:2329`/`2335` (#16), and `record_id` never checked against its region (#17).

PR #13 remains worth landing for what it does prove; it closes the first item on this ticket's desk-proof list, not the ticket.

[R0] **PR #145 retired; original task remains open.**

PR #145 was closed without merge after exact-head external review found that its donor pin also imported the held #69 notification/controller-liveness lane through a partial parent integration. The valid NVM-port result was preserved: 90 checks, 90 PASS at donor merge `44489453`.

Replacement work is tracked by #178, which links the full review and requires a clean re-landing after the integration dependency is settled. This Issue is moved to **On Hold**, not closed; none of its saved-state/persistence acceptance is claimed complete.

[A1] **On Hold**, not closed. PR #145 was closed without merge at exact head `3cb602cc`; the replacement lane is #178.

The hold is on a dependency, not on this ticket's merit: the only submodule pin that carries the NVM power-cut coverage also carries #69's notification and controller-liveness work (13 files, +1448/-200 under donor `hdl/` across `a25b5cc9..44489453`), and #69 / #121 is itself on Hold. #169 states there is no pin that has one without the other. This ticket moves again when #178 has an authorized integration base.

What this lane established and #178 should not re-derive: the donor pin is durable on `protocol-processor` `main`, `tb/nvm_port` reproduces 90/90, and `PINMISSING` on `KL_pp_shadow` is a live gate (0 with all four notification inputs connected, 3 with one removed, naming `ctr_change_i` at `hdl/milan/KL_pp_shadow.sv:864`).

The parent-side persistence gap this ticket is actually about is unchanged: there is still no flash backend, and `A_PP_STAT` still reports a restore that never happened.

[A1] Refined and moved to Ready on the maintainer's instruction of 2026-08-22; #178 (the re-land lane for the nvm_port power-cut coverage) is consolidated here and closed. The pin that carries that coverage (donor `44489453`) is the same one #69 bumps, so this ticket's parent-side work (a real backing store, an honest restore status, the eight persisted items and the binding state) starts once #69's pin is on `dev`.

[A1] **Work item 1 is done and recorded: PR #237.**

`docs/design/SAVED_STATE_FASTCONNECT.md` is restored at the path three source files already cite, and it carries the decision this ticket asked for before implementation.

**The decision.** One image, promoted A/B into the already-reserved raw `journal` slots (`0xEE_0000`, 2 x 64 KiB), with the media owned by the firmware through the LiteSPI master that already exists. The fabric owns the verdict, never the media.

**Measured, since the ticket asked for the area to be weighed first:**

- The whole record set fits one erase block: **31 names x 72 B = 2,232 B** at the shipping 1x1 shape and **235 x 72 B = 16,920 B** at 8x8, so whole-image promotion is comfortable rather than forced.
- The controller is already there: `add_spi_flash(..., with_master=True)` in `milan_soc.py` gives a CSR command master, so write enable, page program and sector erase are reachable from the CPU today. **No new fabric master, no new pads, no area** -- which matters more than usual: #69's pin alone costs +4,396 LUT on the datapath and epic #229 is open against this plane.

**The design problem it solves**, which is the part worth reviewing: the port is a per-record region port with `ERASE_REGION`, the media's smallest erase unit is 64 KiB and two are reserved, and 256 record ids at a block each is the whole device. The port's guarantee is also weaker than the media's -- the donor's own review says the record being rewritten is unprotected and `err` never means the saved set is unchanged. Whole-image A/B above the port closes both.

**Two findings the page records rather than leaving to be rediscovered:**

1. **The silicon-proven writer is gone.** `acmp-persist` drove RDID / WREN / SE-D8 / PP / RDSR against these CSRs on this board, but it lived in a Linux rootfs overlay; the shipping profile is `--flashboot baremetal` and that firmware is one C file that reads flash through the XIP window with **no erase or program path**. The write path must be written again, in the baremetal firmware, against the same CSRs. The sequence is recoverable from git.
2. **Persistence will depend on firmware liveness**, which a fabric master would not. That is the price of re-using the controller, and it is why the page requires `nvm_backed_o` to become evidence-driven -- asserting only after a writer has answered since reset -- instead of today's constant 0. A wedged or absent writer must degrade to an honest "nothing is backed", which is exactly the lie this ticket's title names.

**What is left, and its dependency.** Everything else: the backend, the firmware writer, the mark wiring, the tests. The page's section 8 leaves four things deliberately open (the backend's memory, the backend-to-firmware contract, the debounce window, and DMA versus a CSR window), sized by the decision rather than settled by it. That work starts when #69's pin reaches `dev`, since that is the pin carrying the donor's nvm_port power-cut coverage. This ticket stays open and in progress.

[A1] **Work item 1's decision record was corrected after external review, and two of the corrections change what this ticket asked for.** Recording them here rather than only in the PR, because both are acceptance-affecting. PR #237, head `263151954f87fa622bb357e3d396e74294c574cc`.

## 1. The saved record set did not fit the record namespace, and the design changed

The first version of the decision record sized the persisted set against the 64 KiB erase block, found it fitted, and stopped. It never checked the other capacity in the same design: the processor's NVM port addresses a record by `record_id[7:0]`, so the namespace holds 256 records.

Re-derived from the shipped configs at that head, the full persisted set of this ticket's eight Milan items plus the binding state plus the three design-affirmative items needs **292 records at the 8x8 shape**:

| | 1x1 | 8x8 |
|---|---|---|
| writable names | 31 | 235 |
| everything else (formats, offsets, bindings, maps, rate, clock source, MCR, config index, SUID) | 15 | 57 |
| **total records** | **46** | **292** |
| **highest record id** | 158 | **362**, against 255 |

The 1x1 shape fits, which is why it survived a sizing round that only looked at the shipping default.

**The fix keeps the whole-image A/B decision and changes the namespace inside the image**: fixed id blocks per item group, with the names group banked eight 64-byte name slots to a record. That brings 8x8 to **87 records, highest id `0x9D`, 18,144 bytes**, and it is *cheaper in bytes too* (1,320 bytes saved at 8x8, because 30 record headers replace 235). It costs no landed RTL: the only manager wired to the port today is `KL_acmp_nvm_shadow` (BINDING records, untouched), and the manager that would emit the rest does not exist yet.

`scripts/check_nvm_record_space.py` now gates it for every shipped config, with five negative controls that each redden a different assertion, and it reads the BINDING base out of the donor RTL rather than mirroring it.

## 2. Work item 1's area acceptance is narrowed, in public

Work item 1 says "Measure the area of the flash path before committing". Here is what PR #237 can and cannot deliver, stated as a change to the acceptance rather than smuggled past it.

**Delivered, and settled rather than deferred** (these were previously listed as open):

- **Backend memory: the reserved `ppmem` DRAM window, not BRAM.** Measured: the window is 1,048,576 bytes at `0x7F700000`, holds the 40,000-byte descriptor image and the 4,096-byte response buffer, and the 18,144-byte record image brings it to **under 6 percent** of the reservation. No new reservation, no DTB change. The declined BRAM alternative costs **5 BRAM36** at 8x8.
- **Transfer: ordinary loads and stores**, not DMA and not a CSR data window, because the image is where the CPU can already read it. Only a control tuple crosses the CSR boundary.
- **Zero new flash controller and zero new pads**: the LiteSPI master is already instantiated with `with_master=True`.

**Not delivered, and not deliverable from a documentation-only lane: the backend's own LUT and FF cost.** There is no RTL for the region-to-offset decoder, its main-memory access path or the control CSRs, so there is nothing to synthesise. The first version of the page quoted issue #69's `+4,396 LUT` datapath delta in that slot; that is a different change on a different plane and it has been **removed**, not reinterpreted.

**Proposed acceptance change for work item 1:** it is satisfied by the memory and transfer decisions above with their measured inputs, and the backend's OOC/post-place delta moves to the implementation PR with a named, runnable recipe (`scripts/area_baseline.py --build <after> --compare <before>`, post-place, at both `endstation_ax7101_1x1_tdm8` and `endstation_ax7101_8x8`). If that is not acceptable, the alternative is to hold work item 1 open until the backend RTL exists, which inverts the ticket's own ordering ("decide and record the backing store publicly **before** implementing").

## 3. Three smaller corrections that touch this ticket's acceptance

- **The commit-mark inventory is eight, not three.** Derived from the pinned donor: `SET_SAMPLING_RATE`, `SET_CLOCK_SOURCE`, `SET_CONFIGURATION`, `ADD`/`REMOVE_AUDIO_MAPPINGS`, both `_sfmt` placements (stream format in and out), `SET_STREAM_INFO` (presentation offset) and `SET_NAME`. Work item 4's mutation acceptance now covers all eight independently, plus the deliberate *absence* at `SET_CONTROL` that Milan 5.3.12 requires.
- **`nvm_backed` must be live, not sticky.** An "answered once since reset" bit keeps advertising durable backing after a writer wedges, which is the same false success this ticket exists to remove, just slower. The record now specifies a deadline, a revocation list, and two new bits (`nvm_dirty`, `nvm_stale`) so a wedged writer with data outstanding reads as NOT backed. `docs/reference/REGISTER_MAP.md` owes those rows and a correction to its "`nvm_backed` is a constant" wording when the implementation lands -- that is work item 5.
- **The on-flash container is a new version, KLJ2, not the old KLJ1 carried forward.** KLJ1's records were the deleted plane's register writes and its header carried `n_rec` in eight bits, which is the same limit as item 1 above. The record now pins byte order, field widths, entity and `entity_model_id` binding, CRC coverage, an eleven-row acceptance order with a verdict code per malformed case, and the migration rule.

Ticket stays open for the implementation; nothing here builds anything.

[A1] **Two corrections to what this ticket has been told about work item 1, both acceptance-affecting. PR #237, head `04a836d62df302c4ee324d6aa2ab69df5e63f22c`.**

External review round 2 was NEGATIVE at `c53010c0`. Two of its findings land on this ticket's own acceptance rather than only on the PR, so they are recorded here.

## 1. The area narrowing is WITHDRAWN. Work item 1's measurement is satisfied

My comment of 2026-08-24 14:00 proposed narrowing work item 1's acceptance: the memory and transfer questions settled, the backend's own LUT and FF cost deferred to the implementation PR because "there is no RTL for it".

**That narrowing is withdrawn, and it should never have been proposed.** The review's position was that an executor does not get to rewrite frozen acceptance to make its own Definition of Done green, and that a bound does not need the shipping module -- only a synthesizable candidate. Both are correct.

There is a candidate now, and a measurement. `syn/ooc/sizing/KL_nvm_backend_sizer.sv` carries two tops on the same device face: the blank-flash responder that ships today, lifted verbatim out of `hdl/milan/KL_pp_shadow.sv`, and the backend candidate -- the region-to-offset decoder, the main-memory access path, the control CSRs and the liveness counters.

| top | shape | LUT | FF | RAMB36 | DSP | CARRY4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| blank-flash responder (before) | -- | **35** | 21 | 0 | 0 | 5 |
| backend candidate (after) | 1x1 | **427** | 216 | 0 | 6 | 92 |
| backend candidate (after) | 8x8 | **460** | 216 | 0 | 6 | 90 |
| backend candidate, `-nodsp` | 1x1 | **523** | 216 | 0 | 0 | 118 |
| backend candidate, `-nodsp` | 8x8 | **539** | 216 | 0 | 0 | 116 |

**The backend costs at most 539 LUT and 216 FF**, which is 0.85 percent of the XC7A100T's 63,400 LUT, and the delta over what ships is +504 LUT / +195 FF. Calibrated in the same run: `KL_maap` is 637 LUT / 268 FF and `tcam` is 678 LUT / 1,680 FF, so the backend is smaller than the MAAP engine already in the shipping datapath.

This is an out-of-context upper bound, not a post-place delta -- `syn/yosys/ooc.sh` and `scripts/area_baseline.py` both record why. **So work item 1's "measure the area of the flash path before committing" is met**: the decision is not committing the tight AX7101 shape to an unpriced path any more. The post-place comparison at both shapes stays an obligation on the implementation PR, and the design page's acceptance list now says an in-context delta above 539 LUT means the shipping module diverged from the candidate that was priced.

Reproduce:

```sh
syn/yosys/ooc.sh KL_nvm_blankflash_sizer
OOC_CHPARAM="N_STREAM_IN_P=9 N_STREAM_OUT_P=9 N_SPORT_IN_P=8 N_SPORT_OUT_P=8 \
             N_AUDIO_UNIT_P=1 N_CLK_DOM_P=1 N_NAME_BANK_P=30 MAP_BYTES_P=256" \
  syn/yosys/ooc.sh KL_nvm_backend_sizer
```

## 2. Work item 1 is NOT complete, and this ticket now carries a cross-repository obligation

My comment of 2026-08-24 10:39 said "Work item 1 is done and recorded". **It is not, and that claim is withdrawn too.**

The persisted set needs one record per item group and index -- the pinned donor's F07.8 -- and at the 8x8 shape that is **292 records against a `record_id[7:0]` namespace of 256**. The decision record answered this by banking the user-name group, eight 64-byte name slots per record, and treated the parent's own capacity gate as the tie-breaker against the donor's prose. The review is right that a consumer-side gate cannot override a pinned interface authority, and that no landed donor change or accepted cross-repository decision defines the banked payload.

**No conformant allocation exists**, and the gate now computes that rather than asserting it. F07.8 fixes the record COUNT from the shape, so a perfectly packed conformant allocation would occupy ids `0 .. count-1`; `count > 256` refutes every conformant allocation, not just one layout:

```
endstation_arty_4x4          F07.8 floor= 88/256
endstation_arty_8ch          F07.8 floor=120/256
endstation_arty_current      F07.8 floor= 42/256
endstation_ax7101_1x1_tdm8   F07.8 floor= 46/256
endstation_ax7101_8x8        F07.8 floor=292/256
```

235 of the 292 are Milan 5.3.13 names, and 5.3.13 has no escape clause. So either the donor's record contract is amended or the 8x8 shape cannot be made compliant.

**What this ticket now owes, and to whom:**

| owed by | what | state |
|---|---|---|
| the donor repository | an F07.8 amendment in `07_memory_maps.md` section 5.2: the user-name group is banked, 8 slots of 64 bytes, fixed 512-byte payload, `bank = ordinal / 8`, `slot = ordinal % 8` against the AEMI name-table ordinal, ascending slots, zero-filled tail, all-zero slot means "no name stored" | **NOT filed.** The text is written out verbatim in `docs/design/SAVED_STATE_FASTCONNECT.md` section 4.3, ready to be copied into a donor ticket. Creating an issue in the donor repository was refused by the tooling policy of the environment PR #237 was prepared in |
| this ticket | the pin that carries the amendment, which is #69's pin bump, and only then the promotion of the allocation from PROPOSED to DECIDED | blocked on #69, per this ticket's own frozen sequencing |
| the implementation | a max-shape names bank encoded by one implementation and decoded by the other at the pinned contract, plus a mutation making record index and slot ordinal disagree | in the design page's acceptance list |

Until the first row is discharged, nothing on either side may encode or decode a names bank, PR #237's design page carries the allocation as **PROPOSED** rather than decided, and its Definition of Done box for work item 1 is **unticked**.

## What IS settled by PR #237

So the ticket is not stuck. These parts of work item 1 are decided, recorded and measured, and are not affected by the amendment above:

- **The media and the owner**: one image, promoted A/B into the reserved raw `journal` slots, media owned by the firmware through the LiteSPI master that already exists. The whole set fits one erase block at both shapes under the banked allocation (2,544 B and 18,144 B) **and** under the donor-conformant one (2,696 B and 19,464 B), so this does not depend on the amendment.
- **The container**: KLJ2, byte-level, with the endianness seam, the entity and `entity_model_id` binding, exact CRC-32 coverage and an eleven-row acceptance order with a verdict code per failure.
- **The fabric-side memory and the transfer**: the reserved `ppmem` DRAM window, not BRAM, and ordinary loads and stores, no DMA and no CSR data window. 62,240 of 1,048,576 bytes used, no new reservation, no DTB change.
- **The area**, as above.
- **The durability and liveness contract**, including two deadlines this ticket will be held to: `T-NVM-COMMIT-TIMEOUT` = 8,000 ms, at least 2x the datasheet worst-case commit of 3.37 s at 8x8, and `T-NVM-WRITER-ALIVE` = 2,000 ms with a heartbeat of at most 500 ms that the writer must service during an erase.

Ticket stays open and stays in this lane's scope. Board: In review while PR #237 awaits re-review.

[A1] FINDING — the persisted-format decision that keeps #70 behind donor #24 rests on a premise the tree does not support

The resume conditions recorded on 2026-09-01 put this issue behind donor issue Mister-M-alt/protocol-processor-control-plane-avb-milan#24 (the F07.8 NAMES-bank amendment), "or the parent/donor contracts are amended publicly to remove the dependency". The dependency exists only because `docs/design/SAVED_STATE_FASTCONNECT.md` section 4.3 records, and `scripts/check_nvm_record_space.py` check 6 enforces, the PERSISTED-FORMAT DECISION of 2026-08-25: the banked NAMES layout is retained although no shipped shape forces it any more, "because it is already persisted in flashed boards' KLJ2 images and decoded by landed donor gateware", so a flat re-allocation would be a migration.

Checked against `dev` `25d8ba8b` and the pinned donor `e743dcdc`:

- **No donor gateware decodes a NAMES bank.** `git grep -i 'NAMES_PER_BANK|name.?bank|banked'` over the donor's `hdl/`, `docs/` and tests returns nothing. The donor's F07.8 (`docs/architecture/07_memory_maps.md` section 5.2) still reads "one record per item group and index". `KL_pp_nvm_port` frames a record by `record_id[7:0]` and streams bytes; the only manager wired to it is `KL_acmp_nvm_shadow`, which owns BINDING records. The design page's own status table says the manager for every other persisted item is ABSENT ("lands in P4").
- **No KLJ2 image is written to any board.** The producers and consumers of KLJ2 in the parent are `scripts/nvm_klj2.py`, `scripts/nvm_contract.py`, `scripts/check_nvm_record_space.py`, the sizing candidate `syn/ooc/sizing/KL_nvm_backend_sizer.sv` and its Verilator bench `tb/verilator/nvm_backend`; the submodules mention KLJ2 only in two diagram SVGs. The design page's status table records "A device behind the port: ABSENT" (`NVM_BACKED_C = 1'b0`) and "A write path on the shipping profile: ABSENT"; `sw/firmware/milan_baremetal/` carries no journal, KLJ2, erase or program code; no script or bench tool addresses the `journal` slots at `0xEE_0000`. The slots are reserved in `sw/litex/milan_soc.py` and nothing else touches them.
- **The gate's pass text is stale.** `check_nvm_record_space.py` prints "banking is forced by a shipped shape" in its 0-finding summary while its own floor column shows 164/256 at the worst shape; check 6 passes through the recorded decision, not through necessity.

So there is no persisted image to migrate and no decoder to change. The banked layout is a proposal that costs a cross-repository contract amendment and, at the shapes that ship today, saves 424 bytes at 8x8 (8,800 against 9,224) and 152 at 1x1 (2,544 against 2,696). The donor-conformant flat allocation needs no donor change at all: by the gate's own `--flat` control, one record per item and index gives 164 records and top id `0xEA` at 8x8 and 46 records at 1x1, every image still fits one erase block with margin (14 percent of a slot at worst), and the worst commit is 3.19 s against the 8 s deadline. That control fails today on exactly one finding, check 6's recorded decision.

**Proposal**, to be reviewed rather than assumed: replace the 2026-08-25 decision with the flat, F07.8-conformant allocation; flip check 6 back to the necessity rule (banking is a finding unless a shipped shape forces it) and retarget the `--flat` control; regenerate the sizing bench's record tables; mark section 4.2 DECIDED on the donor's existing contract. That discharges resume condition 1 by its second alternative, leaves donor #24 to be closed as no longer needed, and turns #265 from a persisted-format migration into a re-allocation with nothing to migrate. If a board is known to hold a KLJ2 image, that is the one fact that would reverse this, and it should be named with the board and the image identity.

Nothing in this comment changes the tree; the change lands as a reviewed PR if the proposal stands.

[A1] PR #355 (head `e7c17935`) implements the proposal above: the allocation is the donor's F07.8 rule unchanged, one record per item group and index, each user name one 64-byte record at `0x80 + ordinal` (164 of 256 ids at 8x8, 46 at 1x1); check 6 of `scripts/check_nvm_record_space.py` is the conformance rule, the `--flat` control and the bank-tail check are gone, the sizing candidate and its bench follow (344 and 108 checks, three negative controls red), and section 4.3 of the design page records the history and the reversal. That discharges resume condition 1 of the 2026-09-01 status by its second alternative; conditions 2 to 4 (sequencing with #265, executor and reviewer, the workstation-side power-cycle bench) remain. Card In review.

Step 3 of the plan is up as a PR: the bare-metal flash writer behind `KL_nvm_backend`, graded on a host model per shape. One design decision inside it needs your eye, so it is stated here as well as in the PR.

**The container could not represent a never-written record.** The backend writes the record area in place and erases a record's span to `0xFF`; the firmware wraps that area verbatim; and until the donor's manager exists only binding records are ever written. So every image a board could produce failed section 6.2 rule 12 by construction, and a board that has never been bound could not carry an accepted image at all. The PR adds the **erased-record rule** to section 6.1: a record position may hold its whole span filled with `0xFF`, which counts as present, applies nothing, and restores the vendor default through the processor's own blank arm. It stays narrow: an erased header over a live payload is refused, and an image one record short is still refused. The Python codec, the record-space gate (a sixteenth negative control) and the firmware all implement it, and the firmware's verdicts are cross-checked against the Python decoder's on every case.

**What the writer does**: validates both journal slots at boot, stages the newer accepted container in the reserved window (or an all-erased one), programs the control face, runs the restore walk, heartbeats from the console idle hook, and commits A/B after a provisional 1,000 ms debounce, acknowledging only a slot that verifies. A blank board now reads `blank=1 fail=0 backed=1` instead of `0x5B00_008C`. `milan_nvm [commit|wipe]` on the console.

**What is still open on this issue**: the board proof (a commit observed on the bench, a power cycle, a restore), and the donor-side manager that turns the eight commit marks into records for the seven non-binding Milan items (design page section 12.2). Until that manager lands, an accepted image on a board is binding records and erased spans.

[A10] First persistence proof ON SILICON, 2026-09-21: the BINDING survives a cold power cycle, in both directions. AX7101, dev `f6b31625`, VERSION `0x0002_0060` (the snapshot ownership contract of pull request 491 with the processor's exports wired by pull request 497), three-seed build (best WNS +0.194 ns), flash-pair, UART acceptance 10 of 10 with the fabric gPTP plane locked. Driven from the controller host with raw ACMP; power removed for 8 s at the outlet each time (a cold cycle, never a warm reload).

| Step | Controller reads (GET_RX_STATE, STREAM_INPUT 0) | Firmware console |
|---|---|---|
| fresh image | unbound: talker 0, connection_count 0 | slot A valid seq 1 |
| BIND_RX to a named talker, unique id 3 | SUCCESS; bound to that talker, unique id 3, connection_count 1 | the writer committed on its own: slot B valid **seq 2**, authoritative B, 53 records; commits ok 1, failed 0; backed 1, dirty 0, pending 0; captures refused 0 |
| **cold power cycle** | **bound to the same talker, unique id 3, connection_count 1** | boot walk: offered B seq 2, verdict OK, blank 0, backed 1 |
| UNBIND_RX | SUCCESS; unbound | slot A valid **seq 3**, authoritative A |
| **cold power cycle** | **unbound** (no stale binding resurrected) | boot walk: offered A seq 3, verdict OK |

What this shows: the two-slot image alternates (A, B, A) with a rising sequence; the boot walk picks the newest verified slot; the listener's bound state and its binding parameters (talker entity, talker unique id) come back exactly, which is what Milan v1.2 section 5.5.1.2 requires and what the saved-binding compliance tests power-cycle for; and an unbind is as durable as a bind. The status word read `0xC30000E4` throughout (contract tag `0xC3`, load accepted, backed, nothing pending).

What it does NOT show, and stays open here:
- items 1 to 8 of this issue's list (configuration, sampling rate, stream formats, presentation offset, channel maps, clock source, names): only the BINDING record is materialized today; the rest is the protocol processor's materialization work (scope D3 of `docs/design/SAVED_STATE_SNAPSHOT_OWNERSHIP.md`, its issues 61 and 83);
- a power cut DURING a commit on real flash (the desk suites cover it; a soak with cuts at random phase is the silicon acceptance);
- the started/stopped state and the requesting controller across the cycle, and a real talker answering the restored listener's probe (fast connect);
- the unattended power-cycle soak this issue names as its acceptance test.

Tooling note for whoever repeats it: a raw ACMPDU must carry control_data_length 44; a frame with 52 is dropped by the entity, correctly.
